item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: AI Rout Rattles Markets
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
A post-election slide in chipmakers snowballed as investors bailed from technology shares on speculation that congressional Democrats will clamp down on the artificial-intelligence industry. What started as a rotation out of semiconductor stocks morphed into a broad rout, with all 11 sectors in the S&P 500 Index in the red. Traders caution against interpreting the broader market moves as a fundamental shift in investor preferences.
On today's episode:
Eric Weiner, Bloomberg News Senior Editor Ira Jersey, Bloomberg Intelligence Chief US Rates Strategist Timna Tanners, Wells Fargo Metals & Mining Analyst Tim O'Brien, Bloomberg Opinion Senior Executive Editor (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief: Democrats Map Out Priorities for Next Congress
item.description: Bloomberg's Mario Parker joined the show for, The Debrief, to discuss Democrats' post-midterm focus on lowering costs, rooting out corruption and holding the Trump administration accountable. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Allen Says AI Buildout Already Underway Will Continue
item.description: Allen Says AI data-center projects already underway are unlikely to be disrupted by growing political scrutiny and will bring tens of gigawatts of new compute capacity online over the next 18 months. Allen says 2027 and 2028 will see astonishing growth in AI compute capacity regardless of what happens politically, while future projects could face new requirements around tax breaks, union labor and protections against higher power bills. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Paraguay President Pledges to Defend Himself Before Congress
item.description: Paraguay President Santiago Peña will defend himself in the Senate against a vote to forcibly remove him from office instead of accepting his resignation, a legal distinction that could determine whether he retains immunity from criminal prosecution.
item.dc:creator: Crayton Harrison

item.title: Sarah Bianchi on Market Reaction To Midterm Elections
item.description: Amid a sharp market selloff and a steep drop in semiconductor stocks, Sarah Bianchi discusses concerns that the US midterm election results could lead to tighter constraints on AI infrastructure. She expects delays and says some communities will gain more authority to reject data center projects. In Texas, the incoming Democratic governor has indicated she could move beyond a moratorium if projects include provisions such as no tax incentives, community benefits and local control. Bianchi speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: TC Energy CEO on Data Center Demand After Blue Wave
item.description: TC Energy President & CEO François Poirier, discusses the company as an energy infrastructure provider and referencing its role in data centers and the spin-off of Keystone XL. Poirier stated on a conference call that a Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterms would not undermine the company’s growth plans, and welcomes him to discuss the company’s results. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Dip on Massive Chip Selloff
item.description: Shares of semiconductor stocks plunged on Thursday, extending a recent selloff as investors turn skeptical on the artificial intelligence trade after the Democrats dominated the midterm elections. A team of Bloomberg experts help break down the recent market moves and what comes next, including US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King, US Senior Equities Editor Eric Weiner, Executive Technology Editor Michael Shephard, and Global Head of Tech Research Mandeep Singh. Plus, Equity Research Analyst at Wells Fargo Timna Tanners talks an anticipated steel selloff and how the Midterm results may impact metals industries. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: O'Brien: A Cornered Trump Is a More Volatile Trump
item.description: Democrats delivered a sweeping midterm defeat to Republicans this week, leaving President Trump facing a dramatically different political landscape. Tim O’Brien, Senior Executive Editor for Bloomberg Opinion, looks at Trump’s history under pressure, the coming clash with a Democratic Congress, and what it could mean for the final two years of his presidency. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Take: The Economic Policy Dems Can Do Without Trump
item.description: The Blue Wave might have been a rebuke of Trump and his economy, but Democrats have limited options to tackle affordability without him. On today’s Big Take podcast, PIMCO’s Head of Public Policy Libby Cantrill joins host Sarah Holder to discuss how the economic issues Democrats campaigned on could translate into policy and the compromises and clashes that may lie ahead. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Governor-Elect Requests Pause on SpaceX Land Talks
item.description: Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa used her first news conference since winning election to spotlight her scrutiny of the potential sale of state park land to Elon Musk’s Space Exploration Technologies Corp.
item.dc:creator: Joe Lovinger and Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Why Is Everyone Leaving New Zealand?
item.description: Billionaires may be flocking to New Zealand, but its working-age population is leaving in droves. Many are professionals with friends and family headed to Australia. So what’s driving this exodus? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Meets Putin Envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House
item.description: President Donald Trump said he met with Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House but did not visit with Ukrainian representatives.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Hegseth Expands National Guard Presence in Washington DC
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is expanding the controversial National Guard presence in Washington, DC, giving troops the ability to use dozens of patrol cars, military tactical vehicles, National Guard boats and other assets in the nation’s capital.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Natalia Drozdiak

item.title: First Jobs Report After Midterms Could Show the Challenge Ahead
item.description: How much can the Democrats do to change the conditions that helped sweep them into power?
item.dc:creator: Mark Niquette

item.title: Carney Spends Canada’s Oil Windfall in Bid to Drive Growth
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney doubled down on his plan to use the government’s balance sheet to spur an investment boom in Canada, increasing borrowing and using a surge of tax revenue to plow billions into expanding the productive capacity of the economy.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt and Erik Hertzberg

item.title: Rubio Weighs Leaving Administration After GOP’s Midterm Loss
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is weighing whether to leave the Trump administration, people familiar with the matter said, as he considers his next moves following Republicans’ midterm elections wipeout this week.
item.dc:creator: Saleha Mohsin, Natalia Drozdiak, Eric Martin and Annmarie Hordern

item.title: Hegseth to Face Impeachment Vote as Early as Next Week
item.description: US lawmakers are looking to impeach embattled Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as soon as next week, an effort that’s gained momentum after the Iran war he championed partly led to Republicans losing control of Congress in the midterms.
item.dc:creator: Roxana Tiron and Erik Wasson

item.title: Cuba Detains Opposition Journalist Yoani Sánchez in ‘Alarming’ Crackdown
item.description: Yoani Sánchez, one of Cuba’s best-known independent reporters, was detained by state security amid a broader crackdown on critics of the island’s communist government.
item.dc:creator: Jim Wyss

item.title: Paraguay President Peña Resigns After Ueno Bank Collapse
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation Thursday after the collapse of a major commercial bank with ties to his government plunged the South American nation into turmoil.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias and Ken Parks

item.title: Democratic Socialist Raman Wins LA Mayor Race, Bass Concedes
item.description: Los Angeles City Councilmember Nithya Raman won the mayor’s race, ousting incumbent Karen Bass and putting a democratic socialist in charge of the second-largest US city.
item.dc:creator: John Gittelsohn
